content: The following regimens are excluded from the analyses: 1. Short regimens without bedaquiline and not conforming to WHO (2020) recommendations: Individuals receiving these regimens are excluded from comparative analyses because they lack bedaquiline, a drug considered one of the most effective components in treating multidrug-resistant or rifampin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB). 2. Short-course regimens including bedaquiline and an injectable agent: Individuals initially treated with injectable antibiotics before transitioning to a bedaquiline-containing regimen are excluded from comparative analyses, as these regimens do not comply with the WHO 2020 Guidelines. Note: Regimens described as 12-month regimens include any treatment duration up to 365 days. The term 9–12 months is consistent with the nomenclature used in the WHO 2020 consolidated treatment guidelines. Fluoroquinolone antibiotics: These are integral to standardized treatment for MDR/RR-TB as per the 2019 WHO guidelines and the 2020 consolidated guidelines. To align with WHO recommendations, a fluoroquinolone (e.g., levofloxacin or moxifloxacin) must be included unless resistance to fluoroquinolones has been demonstrated. Eligibility for inclusion in the evidence review: Data included in this review were identified by the WHO Global TB Program in 2021 following a public call for data. These datasets include clinical trials and patient cohorts treated for MDR/RR-TB between April 2017 and December 2021. Criteria for dataset inclusion: 1. Data from clinical trials (with or without comparator groups) or programmatic cohorts of MDR/RR-TB patients. 2. At least 25 patients must have completed treatment with an assigned end-of-treatment outcome. 3. Included patients must have MDR/RR-TB. 4. Treatment regimen composition and duration must be determinable, with sufficient data to assign treatment outcomes for most participants. 5. Patients must be treated with an intervention or comparator regimen relevant to the review. Eligibility of participants for inclusion: Within included datasets, patients must meet the following criteria: 1. Bacteriologically confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis (via PCR or culture). 2. Rifampin resistance (± isoniazid resistance) confirmed by phenotypic or genotypic drug susceptibility testing within 365 days prior to treatment initiation. 3. Treatment regimen composition and duration must be clearly defined. 4. For PICO questions involving fluoroquinolone status, baseline fluoroquinolone resistance status must be available. Outcomes to be analyzed: WHO-directed PICO questions list the following treatment outcomes: 1. Cured. 2. Treatment completed. 3. Treatment failed. 4. Death (any cause). 5. Lost to follow-up. 6. Adverse events (including drug-drug interactions for HIV-infected patients). 7. Amplification (acquisition) of drug resistance. Outcome definitions: Standardized definitions will be applied wherever possible, following WHO guidelines adopted in November 2020. Treatment success will combine cure and treatment completed outcomes. Sustained treatment success will be defined as no documented relapse by the date of censoring. Comparative analyses: Comparative analyses will be conducted within individual studies and across multiple studies. Pairwise comparisons will be performed for short-course regimens (e.g., 6-month regimens) and relevant comparators. An individual patient data (IPD) network meta-analysis will be conducted where multiple studies share common comparator groups, enabling ranking of regimens after adjusting for participant characteristics. Statistical methods: Outcomes will be presented as unadjusted and adjusted risk ratios. Adjusted risk ratios will be calculated using log-binomial generalized linear regression with inverse probability propensity score weighting. If convergence issues arise, Poisson regression with robust variance estimation or logistic regression for odds ratios will be used. Sensitivity analyses: Additional sensitivity analyses will evaluate the impact of eligibility criteria and follow-up times on outcomes. These include follow-up durations of 12 and 18 months, as well as bestand worst-case mortality scenarios for cohorts with incomplete follow-up data. Stratification: Effect estimates will be stratified by characteristics such as fluoroquinolone resistance, smear status, cavitation on chest X-ray, HIV status, baseline culture status, age, smoking, and diabetes. Limitations and potential biases: Comparative analyses within randomized trial populations are less likely to be affected by unmeasured confounding. However, comparisons between trials may be influenced by differences in participant characteristics, programmatic settings, standards of care, and timing of diagnosis. Incomplete data may also pose limitations in some datasets. Exploratory analyses: Additional analyses may be conducted to explore the effects of drug duration, adherence measures, and treatment toxicity on outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluding participants with missing resistance profiles may also be performed. Missing data: Multiple imputation by chained equations will be used to address missing data for potential confounders when the proportion of missing values is less than 45%. For missing drug susceptibility test results, susceptibility will be assumed unless resistance is documented (except for rifampin, where evidence of resistance is required).
